name: Prize crossword No 22,231
preamble: Subsidiary parts of all clues ignore (appropriately) the last clue; definitions are normal.

clue.text: Two universities with one book about Zorba the Greek's instrument

indicators.note: the book is wrapped about the other letters, so they sit inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university, twice over
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A recipe for building the instrument heard in the film Zorba the Greek, out of colleges and a book.
explanation.walkthrough: One U goes after each O of BOOK, making BOUOUK, and I follows. The preamble's ignored Z then goes back in to give the grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The bouzouki, a long-necked Greek lute, plays the famous dance tune in the film Zorba the Greek.

clue.text: Entire range where an extremist will stop?

blocks.note: first meaning: everything, from beginning to end
second meaning, cryptically: someone who goes to the very end of the alphabet runs all the way to its last letter

explanation.surface: The whole spectrum, ending wherever a fanatic finally draws the line.
explanation.walkthrough: An extremist goes as far as possible, so in alphabet terms they run the whole way, stopping at the final letter, which is exactly the letter this puzzle keeps out of its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes covering everything comprehensively, like a street atlas indexing every road in alphabetical order.

clue.text: Heading from the grave; that is a snake god

indicators.note: taking the heading from a word means its first letter is cut away

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
a grave is a tomb
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Something rises headfirst out of a grave, and it turns out to be a serpent deity.
explanation.walkthrough: As the preamble warns, the wordplay ignores Z: it gives OMBIE, and the grid adds the Z back. The surface's 'heading from the grave' suggests a zombie, which is the answer by another route.
explanation.definitionFit: In voodoo belief, zombie (or zombi) is also the name of the python deity worshipped in West African and Haitian rites.

clue.text: Crossed with a horse, initially enormous, medium for tuna, perhaps?

definitions.note: an adjective-like phrase for a noun: the zebrine is the hybrid of a zebra crossed with a horse

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows it

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
the first letter of enormous
tuna is often canned in brine, the salty liquid it is kept in

explanation.surface: A puzzling list of traits: a horse cross, something enormous, and the liquid round a tin of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' here is the liquid something is packed in, not a psychic or a size.
explanation.definitionFit: Zebrine names the hybrid foal produced when a zebra is bred with a horse, as well as meaning zebra-like.

clue.text: White or spoiled, weapon for an angled shot

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined and knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.surface: Something white, or perhaps spoiled, is offered as a weapon for firing at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives HOWITER and the grid restores the ignored Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is an artillery gun that fires shells on a high, steep trajectory, lobbing them over obstacles.

clue.text: All the time, order turning up  ...  on pizza?

definitions.note: a phrase saying where the cheese goes, standing for the noun

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: taken as written
an era is a period of time
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
the letters every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.surface: Someone keeps sending back their order, all the time, with a hint of what topping they want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the time' looks like a single phrase meaning always, but it splits into two pieces. The ellipsis just carries the surface on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozzarella is the soft Italian cheese that tops a classic pizza, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Runner has time once spent in Constantinople

blocks.note: a runner bean is a climbing bean, so a runner is a bean
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An athlete takes a while and is long past, back in old Byzantium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is the garden vegetable. The ignored Z sits inside BEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The bezant was a gold coin of the Byzantine Empire, the currency once used in its capital, Constantinople.

clue.text: Wheel of life decapitates, say, William Blake (painter)

indicators.note: cutting off the head of a word removes its first letter

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
William Blake is an example of a poet, as 'say' signals
a painter is a rope for tying up a small boat

explanation.surface: A grisly scene in which a wheel beheads William Blake, oddly described as a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake was also a painter, which makes 'painter' look like a description of him; it is the nautical rope. Zoetrope literally means 'wheel of life' in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoetrope is a Victorian spinning drum whose slits make pictures appear to move; its name comes from Greek for life and turning.

clue.text: Former London dialing code's a gas

blocks.note: London's old telephone code was 01, read aloud as letters
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A remark that London's old telephone prefix was a hoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Until 1990 the London code was 01, which spells O plus ONE; the ignored Z goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, a pale blue gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Iraqi minister's first-class

blocks.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 written as I
the letters every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.surface: Praise for an Iraqi government minister as top-notch.
explanation.walkthrough: With the Zs ignored, AZIZ shrinks to just AI, the crossword's usual A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariq Aziz served as Iraq's foreign minister and deputy prime minister under Saddam Hussein.

clue.text: A few notes have detailed little boy's regression at coming of age

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut off
a regression is a going backwards, so these letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a bar of music holds a few notes
taken as written
Tiny Tim is the little boy in A Christmas Carol
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A boy celebrating turning thirteen regresses while a few musical notes play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regression' covers both the shortened word and the boy together, not just the boy. Tiny Tim from A Christmas Carol is the crossword's stock little boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar mitzvah is the Jewish ceremony marking a boy's religious adulthood at thirteen, his coming of age.

clue.text: Setter not given a quarter for his work

indicators.note: the setter is denied the letter named, so that letter is dropped from his name

blocks.note: Paul is the setter of this crossword
the letters every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A setter complains that he is not paid even a quarter of what his work deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Paul himself; PAUL loses its A to give PUL, then E follows. Restoring the two ignored Zs gives the grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword setter's product is a puzzle, so the thing Paul works at is exactly this word.

clue.text: Deviancy - one desperate for it!

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
the Roman numeral for one
British slang: someone gagging for it is desperate to have it
the second ignored Z

explanation.surface: A cheeky jibe that deviancy is what one desperate person wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gagging for it' is British slang for being desperately keen. Deviancy here is deviating, swerving from a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: Zigzagging is constantly veering off course from side to side, a literal form of deviating from a straight path.

clue.text: Singers King Cole and Franklin wanting a home for Jesus

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter named is missing from the end

blocks.note: Nat King Cole was an American singer; 'Singers' covers him and Franklin
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
Aretha Franklin was the American soul singer

explanation.surface: Two famous singers find themselves short of something as they look for the town where Jesus grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: NAT and ARETHA, losing ARETHA's final A, give NATARETH, so the grid's Z stands where NAT's T would be rather than being simply added; the clue does not account for losing the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazareth in Galilee is the town where Jesus was brought up, which is why he is called Jesus of Nazareth.

clue.text: Dizzy girls providing backing for rock concerts

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so this word is written in reverse

blocks.note: if means providing, as in 'providing it rains'
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
gigs are live music performances

explanation.surface: Giddy young women are singing backing vocals at rock shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providing backing' looks like a phrase about backing singers; 'backing' alone reverses 'providing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizgig is an old word for a flighty, frivolous girl, so fizgigs are giddy young women.

clue.text: Complain about the state of the Chechen capital

indicators.note: the complaint goes about, around, the state, holding it inside

blocks.note: to groan is to grumble or complain
NY is New York, an American state
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A grumble about conditions in Chechnya's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The state' sounds like the condition of the city; it is New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Groznyan is the adjective for Grozny, capital city of the Russian republic of Chechnya, describing what relates to it.

clue.text: English on their toes about Loire valley town

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the phrase's word is written backwards

blocks.note: people on their toes are alert
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: English visitors stay on their toes as they wander about a French river town.
explanation.walkthrough: The English E is written last, after the reversed ALERT and the ignored Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Trélazé is a small town near Angers in the Maine-et-Loire department, known for slate quarries in the Loire valley.

clue.text: Show Scotsmen to be Africans

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
to air something is to show it in public
Ian is the Scottish form of John, so Scotsmen are Ians

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to prove that some Scottish men are actually from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian is the stock Scottish man's name in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Zairians were the people of Zaire, the name the Democratic Republic of the Congo used from 1971 to 1997.

clue.text: Vitality of father beginning to abate

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
the letters every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
the first letter of abate
two more of the ignored letter

explanation.surface: A father's energy is starting to fade with age.
explanation.walkthrough: With all four Zs ignored, a seven-letter word shrinks to just PA and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pazzazz, more often spelt pizzazz, is lively energy and flair, the same sparkle as vitality.

clue.text: Spanish region's not completed a former capital of that region

indicators.note: something not completed is left unfinished, so its final letter is missing

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
Aragon is a region of north-east Spain
the second ignored Z
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note that a Spanish region is unfinished, and that a city was once its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That region' makes the definition point back to the wordplay's Aragon, so the clue reads naturally as one statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaragoza, also called Saragossa, was the capital of the medieval Kingdom of Aragon and remains the region's main city.

clue.text: Fern Scottish town uprooted

indicators.note: in a down clue, something pulled up by the roots comes out upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: Alloa is a town in central Scotland, near Stirling
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A fern is dug up from a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprooted' suits the fern, but it is the town that is pulled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Azolla is a genus of tiny floating water ferns, often called mosquito fern or fairy moss.

clue.text: Don't take away food for plant hormone

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
eating in is the opposite of taking a takeaway home

explanation.surface: A café instruction not to take food out, oddly addressed to a plant hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: The café question 'eat in or take away?' supplies EAT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeatin is a cytokinin, a plant growth hormone first isolated from maize kernels, that promotes cell division.

clue.text: See 26
Mistakenly ignore God and be turned to stone

indicators.note: doing something mistakenly means getting it wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.surface: A warning that anyone who wrongly ignores God will be punished by being petrified.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Lot's wife, punished for disobeying God by being turned into a pillar of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a Gorgon such as Medusa petrified anyone who looked at her, so to gorgonize is to petrify.

clue.text: A Teutonic maize protein

explanation.walkthrough: Teutonic means German, so 'a' is translated into German.
explanation.definitionFit: Zein is the chief storage protein of corn kernels, used in coatings, inks and food glazes.

clue.text: My boss is sound asleep

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

is contracts to 's

explanation.surface: An office worker reports that the boss is fast asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound asleep' means deeply asleep on the surface, but is read as the noise of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeds are the snoring noises cartoons write as a row of Zs, the sound made when asleep.

clue.text: Tenor Turner

blocks.note: Lana Turner was the Hollywood film star
the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' could be a lathe worker or the painter; it is the actress, and the ignored Z goes in before her final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Mario Lanza was an American operatic tenor and film star of the 1950s, famous for The Great Caruso.

clue.text: Home game's ending for Germany and the same for Italy and Scandinavian World Cup hero

indicators.note: a word's ending is its last letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: the letter every clue's wordplay leaves out, as the preamble says
someone at home is in
the last letter of game
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
the same two pieces again, home and the game's ending
the second ignored Z
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
a Dane is a Scandinavian from Denmark

explanation.surface: A footballer celebrated for a home win over Germany, then Italy, and a Scandinavian side.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'for' marks a country's international vehicle code following IN plus E. As the last clue, this one names the letter the whole puzzle ignores: its hero's initials are both Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinedine Zidane scored twice in the 1998 final to win France the World Cup, making him a national hero.
